Plan outline:

A. Target semantics
- `make PLATFORM=... coverage` end-to-end: separate variant `...-cov`, force CONFIG=debug, SANITIZE=none, LINK=obj; stop on test failure; report.
- `COVERAGE=1` remains axis for direct instrumented runs.
- Not part of `all`/`test`.

B. Build layer
- GCC: `-fprofile-arcs -ftest-coverage -fprofile-abs-path` compile, `--coverage` link.
- MSVC: if static route: `/PROFILE` link for coverage; /Zi already.
- Auto defaults for SANITIZE/LINK when COVERAGE=1.

C. Execution model
- dispatcher recursion: outer `coverage` -> sub-make COVERAGE=1.
- `cov-inputs` builds lib/exes/ref data (no app runs).
- `cov-reset` removes .gcda/.coverage/markers so tests truly rerun.
- run `unit acceptance` under collector (Windows) / normally (Linux).
- postcondition: all markers exist + report exists; otherwise fail. Explicit test of collector exit code during spike.

D. Windows specifics
- tool discovery via vswhere, overridable CODE_COVERAGE.
- `collect --output ... -- $(MAKE) ...` with `--` separator.
- settings XML for source excludes and (if static) IncludeDirectories; generated in build dir.
- merge -> Cobertura XML.
- spike: dynamic native first; fallback static /PROFILE.

E. Linux specifics

parts.text:
What do unit test exes include? TASK_template test links `core_srcs` = all task sources except main. So task unit tests don't cover main. Unit-only coverage = common + task core (arg parsing, patterns, stats, filter). Good. Acceptance later adds main.

Interesting: task 4 has no core srcs? filter.c maybe. Check. Not needed.

Windows coverage: test exes are built with LINK=obj; static libs not used for tests (module_inputs static => because LINK=obj, module_inputs obj returns MODULE_OBJS). So common objects are directly linked into test exes, not static lib. Good, /PROFILE on link of test exes covers them.

If wrapping `make unit` with collector and settings IncludeDirectories pointing at BUILD_DIR recursively, it instruments test exes only (apps not built). But `cov-inputs` if it builds `exes` would build apps too; better build only test exes: `$(UNIT_EXES)`. There's `TEST_$1_$2` variables; marker deps. Need a list `UNIT_EXES`. Currently `ALL_EXES` includes apps+tests+refs. Add `ALL_TESTS` list when eval template, or use `$(patsubst %.passed,%,$(UNIT_MARKERS))`? UNIT_MARKERS = `...passed`; base exe is `.../<name>(.exe)`; pattern `%.passed` -> `%` gives path without extension, and on Windows exe has `.exe` before `.passed`: `ppm_io_test.exe.passed`? Let's inspect: `TEST_$1_$2 := .../name$(EXE)`, `UNIT := $(patsubst %$(EXE),%,TEST).passed` => on Windows `name.passed` (EXE stripped), then dependency is `TEST` (name.exe). So UNIT marker is `name.passed`, not `name.exe.passed`. On Linux same. So `$(patsubst %.passed,%$(EXE),$(UNIT_MARKERS))` gives exes. Could define `UNIT_EXES` in template. Simpler add `UNIT_EXES += $$(TEST_$1_$2)` inside template. Fine.

Then `cov-inputs: $(UNIT_EXES) $(STATIC_LIB...)`? Unit exes depend on module inputs; on LINK=obj no lib. Common test exes defined separately; add them. Need `COV_UNIT_EXES := $(UNIT_EXES) $(BUILD_DIR)/common/c/ppm_io_test$(EXE) $(BUILD_DIR)/common/cpp/ppm_io_test$(EXE)`. Could define a phony `cov-inputs: $(UNIT_MARKERS)`? No, markers run tests. Dependency of markers is the exe; but phony target can depend on `$(patsubst %.passed,%$(EXE),$(UNIT_MARKERS))`.

Then reset: `cov-reset` removes `$(UNIT_MARKERS)` and `*.coverage` and `$(COV_DIR)`. On GCC removes `.gcda`. But `cov-reset` must be run in sub-make after build; it doesn't require compiler. If `cov-reset` is a target in sub-make, it needs path variables. Good.

Windows coverage flow:
- outer `coverage`:
```
coverage:
	$(MAKE) PLATFORM=$(PLATFORM) ... COVERAGE=1 cov-inputs
	$(MAKE) PLATFORM=... COVERAGE=1 cov-reset
	$(call COV_RUN, $(MAKE) PLATFORM=... COVERAGE=1 unit)
	$(MAKE) PLATFORM=... COVERAGE=1 cov-report
```
But `$(call COV_RUN,...)` on Windows needs quoting and native paths.

Alternative simpler: make coverage target in sub-make mode, and outer dispatcher only:
```
ifeq ($(COVERAGE),0)
coverage:
	$(MAKE) ... COVERAGE=1 coverage
else
coverage: cov-inputs cov-reset cov-run cov-report
...
endif
```
But `cov-reset` as prerequisite of coverage runs possibly in parallel with cov-inputs under -j (bad: reset markers before/parallel). Use recursive recipe lines instead of prerequisites:
```
coverage:
	$(MAKE) ... COVERAGE=1 cov-inputs
	$(MAKE) ... COVERAGE=1 cov-reset
	$(MAKE) ... COVERAGE=1 cov-run
	$(MAKE) ... COVERAGE=1 cov-report
```
Each line sequential. But `cov-run` in sub-make runs tests under collector; can define `cov-run` recipe that invokes collect around `$(MAKE) COVERAGE=1 unit`. That's nested. Could instead have the outer line wrap the sub-make directly:
```
	$(call COV_RUN,$(MAKE) ... COVERAGE=1 unit)
```
Then `cov-report` separate sub-make. This is fine.

But note: Windows `collect` static instrumention needs settings with IncludeDirectories. Generate settings file in `cov-inputs` (after build) or `cov-reset`. We can generate with `echo` lines? Could avoid file generation by using `instrument` per exe. Let's reconsider settings generation difficulty. Actually maybe Make can write the file via `$(file >...)` GNU make function! GNU make 4.0+ has `$(file >file,text)` which writes file at parse time or recipe expansion. Use in recipe: `$(file >$(COV_DIR)/coverage.runsettings,<?xml ...?>)`. But multi-line content with commas and XML — the `$(file ...)` function separates text after comma; commas in text are fine (only first comma separates, rest is text). Newlines? Can't easily embed newlines in make variable? You can define a multiline variable with `define`. Then `$(file >$@,$(COV_SETTINGS))`. That writes at recipe expansion. Nice, portable, no shell quoting. GNU make 4.4 supports. This is a good technique. Or generate at parse time via `$(file >...)` only when coverage requested; but writing at parse time also okay. Better in recipe.

However settings file needs absolute path? If relative `build/...` maybe resolved from CWD; make runs repo root. Could use `$(CURDIR)` (make built-in) converted to native path. `$(CURDIR)` is absolute with `/` on Windows? GNU make on Windows CURDIR uses `C:/...`. The tool expects Windows path; `/` accepted by .NET XML? Likely. Use `$(subst /,\,$(CURDIR)/$(BUILD_DIR))` via native. Could test.

Alternatively settings only needs `<Sources><Exclude>` for tests; `collect` static C++ requires IncludeDirectories to know what to instrument. Could use `--include-files` with explicit test exe paths instead of settings? `-if` list of files to statically instrument, maybe accepts multiple paths. If so, pass all unit test exe paths; no settings needed for include, but still need settings for source excludes. Could skip source exclude initially and accept test files in report? Not ideal; coverage of test code inflates. Better settings.

Actually maybe `instrument` command doesn't need settings: instrument each unit exe in place before running `make unit`, then uninstrument after. Then no IncludeDirectories. But we'd still need Sources exclude for report; could pass settings to `instrument` (applies at instrumentation) or `collect`. If instrument runs without settings, test sources included. We could post-filter? Hmm.

Simplest robust: one settings XML with IncludeDirectories + Sources exclude, used by collect around `make unit`. Generate via `$(file ...)`.

Does `collect` static instrumentation of all exes in IncludeDirectories work when command is make? It instruments before running command. All test exes exist. Then make runs them; instrumented exes report. Good.

Need confirm `collect` returns child exit code. Test now? We can run a read-only-ish spike: cover an existing exe? Existing debug exes maybe not built. `build/msvc-...dll-address` exists. It might contain exes. Running collect would create output.coverage in CWD — that's a file modification, forbidden in plan mode. Could set output to temp outside workspace (allowed temp dir), but collect would statically instrument exe on disk (modifies build artifact, restores). Still a system change, prohibited. So no spike now. Plan includes spike during implementation.

Now user says they used collect + /PROFILE; we should trust that static route works. So skip dynamic experimentation? They explicitly said used /PROFILE. Plan should adopt /PROFILE + collect static. Could still verify exit code/report during implementation, but not make it a decision spike. Good—less uncertainty.

Now "coverage должен в идеале работать всегда": If `coverage` target depends on /PROFILE variant and environment, requires vcvars (already required for cl). Good. On Linux requires gcovr. "Всегда" perhaps means not gated behind weird manual steps. We'll make it self-contained.

Answer "why not debug version": clarify we use CONFIG=debug; separate dir because /PROFILE link flag and ASan. They said flags not much differ—true. But if we reuse the *same* debug dir, then /PROFILE would have to be in normal debug link; and coverage run instruments binaries in place. Since static instrumentation modifies exe on disk, doing that to the regular debug artifacts is risky but restorable. More importantly ASan must be off. The existing variant model already creates `-cov`; using it is consistent with AGENTS §4.7 ("отдельная сборка"). So separate variant.

Could we allow coverage on an already-built debug variant without /PROFILE? No, static requires /PROFILE. Dynamic might, but user validated static.

Now "несовместимые цели - согласен" — they agree exclusions (coverage only debug/none/obj). Good.

"coverage должен работать всегда" maybe also means no `COVERAGE=1` knob needed; target does everything. Yes.

"пока unit, затем acceptance" — plan adjust: cov-inputs builds only unit test exes; report covers core+common; main not covered. Explicitly state this limitation. Add an extension point: later acceptance adds app exes and main coverage; design shouldn't block it.

"README убираем" — no docs changes until validation. Plan: code only Makefile + maybe settings generated. No README/AGENTS/CHANGELOG. If a new helper file is needed (settings template), add? They said only after validation for docs. A settings template is code/build config, could be generated; no separate doc.

"Валидация решений на мне" — our plan should include "предлагаемые проверки", not claim validation. In implementation, we might run make to ensure it functions; but user says validation on them. We'll state we'll run smoke check only if they permit? We generally need verify solution. But instruction says user validates decisions. We'll implement and report commands for them; maybe run compile/lint? Makefile no lint. I'd say: implementation includes checking `make -n` and one actual run? They might want to do it. Better: in plan, "проверку выполняешь ты; я в реализации ограничиваюсь статической проверкой Makefile (`make -n`) и не трогаю документацию". But we should ensure it works. Hmm. They said "Валидация решений - тоже на мне" — decisions, not necessarily build smoke tests. We can run build/test to catch errors, but final acceptance theirs. Keep plan: "я прогоняю smoke, финальную валидацию и правки документации делаешь ты". Or avoid overpromising.

Now, need clarify one thing: What does the user mean "в отладке пройти по интересующим тест-кейсам"? They might want to debug the *coverage build* under cdb. Coverage variant is Debug config, so cdb works (symbols /Zi, /Od). But /PROFILE may affect? Should be fine. So answer: coverage variant is fully debuggable; separate dir doesn't lose that. You can set breakpoints in instrumented binaries? Static instrumentation rewrites the binaries; does it preserve PDB line mapping/debug info? It may break debugging? Hmm. If statically instrumented on disk, the binary differs from pdb; debugging can be odd. But collect restores binaries after run; during run instrumented. Debugging instrumented exe under cdb may not map perfectly. However the normal debug variant remains for step-through. So: use `make ... debug` build for cdb, coverage variant for reporting. That's an answer. If they want to debug while collecting, could run normal debug variant under cdb and collect? Static requires /PROFILE which normal debug lacks. They could build debug with /PROFILE and collect dynamically? Hmm. Let's not overcomplicate: coverage build is Debug-like, so cdb attach possible, but instrumented binaries are rewritten during collection. The recommendation: debug on normal debug variant; coverage variant for numbers.

Wait: /PROFILE is link-time and static instrumentation happens at collect time by rewriting exe. If they want to run under cdb *with coverage collection*, they'd need instrumentation. But for "пройти по интересующим тест-кейсам" they can use normal debug build with the same test exe and set breakpoints; the source and flags match coverage build. So separate dirs don't hinder. Good.

Now, "coverage должен в идеале работать всегда" could also mean make coverage should not depend on `COVERAGE=1` being typed; dispatcher handles. Confirm.

Now refine implementation plan specifics with Makefile details:

1. Defaults:
```
SANITIZE ?= $(if $(filter 1,$(COVERAGE)),none,$(SANITIZE_DEFAULT_$(CONFIG)))
LINK ?= $(if $(filter 1,$(COVERAGE)),obj,lib)
```
But order: COVERAGE defined after SANITIZE currently. Move COVERAGE definition above SANITIZE. Fine.

2. Coverage flags:
MSVC:
```
PROFILE := $(if $(filter 1,$(COVERAGE)),-PROFILE)
LDFLAGS := -nologo -DEBUG $(PROFILE) $(LDFLAGS_$(CONFIG))
```
Check MSVC flag spelling: link option is `/PROFILE` (dash accepted: `-PROFILE`). Good.
GCC:
```
COV_GCC := $(if $(filter 1,$(COVERAGE)),-fprofile-arcs -ftest-coverage -fprofile-abs-path)
FLAGS_c := ... $(COV_GCC)
FLAGS_cpp := ... $(COV_GCC)
LDFLAGS := ... $(if COVERAGE, --coverage)
```
`--coverage` implies -lgcov at link. Also compile flag `--coverage` would be equivalent; use explicit.

Need ensure GCC `-fprofile-abs-path` valid (GCC 8+). Confidence high.

3. Variant already `-cov`.

4. `coverage` target only valid in dispatcher mode? If COVERAGE=0 and user runs `make coverage`:
- if we keep `coverage` recipe as recursive dispatcher, and `COVERAGE=1` sub-make also has `coverage` target -> infinite recursion unless guarded. Define:
```
ifeq ($(COVERAGE),1)
coverage: cov-run ...
else
coverage:
	$(MAKE) ... COVERAGE=1 coverage
endif
```
But passing SANITIZE/LINK: with auto defaults, if outer LINK=lib default, propagating LINK=lib explicit would break. Don't propagate SANITIZE/LINK/CONFIG unless user set? Standard make command-line vars propagate via MAKEFLAGS automatically! If user ran `make PLATFORM=windows coverage`, only PLATFORM is command-line; sub-make gets PLATFORM via MAKEFLAGS; CONFIG/SANITIZE/LINK are file defaults, recomputed in sub-make with COVERAGE=1 (if we pass COVERAGE=1 as command-line). Good. But `TOOLCHAIN ?= $(TOOLCHAIN_$(PLATFORM))` recomputes. GCC_SUFFIX etc. propagate if command line. So sub-make invocation just `$(MAKE) COVERAGE=1 coverage` (plus PLATFORM already in MAKEFLAGS). But `make coverage` without PLATFORM errors in outer before passing; fine.
- If user explicitly passes `SANITIZE=address`, it propagates via MAKEFLAGS and exclusion errors in sub-make. Good.
- If user explicitly passes `LINK=lib`, propagates and errors. With auto default only when not explicit. Good.
- If user passes `CONFIG=release`, propagates and exclusion errors. Good.
So dispatcher: `$(MAKE) COVERAGE=1 coverage`. Perfect, "works always" by defaults.

But the recursive sub-make also sees `MAKECMDGOALS=coverage`, and `COVERAGE=1` branch. Need branch based on `COVERAGE`.

5. Flow in COVERAGE=1 mode:
```
coverage: 
	$(MAKE) COVERAGE=1 cov-inputs
	$(MAKE) COVERAGE=1 cov-reset
	<collect> $(MAKE) COVERAGE=1 unit
	$(MAKE) COVERAGE=1 cov-report
```
Nested recursion again. Each sub-make gets COVERAGE=1 command-line and coverage goal? We pass explicit goal `cov-inputs`, so fine. But when sub-make invoked with `COVERAGE=1 cov-inputs`, MAKECMDGOALS no longer coverage, so no branch issue.

Could avoid nested by making `coverage` prerequisites with `.NOTPARALLEL`? Simpler nested lines as above. GNU make treats lines with `$(MAKE)` as recursive and executes sequentially. Without `+`, make recognizes `$(MAKE)` and passes jobserver, and under `-n` executes the sub-make (documented). Fine.

However each recipe line runs in a separate cmd shell, so the collector line must be one command:
```
	"$(COVERAGE_TOOL)" collect --nologo --settings $(native settings) --output $(native out.coverage) --format cobertura -- $(MAKE) COVERAGE=1 unit
```
Need `--` before command. Does collect accept `-f cobertura` directly? `collect -f` supported. Use `.coverage` then merge for VS? For unit-only, direct cobertura is enough; but binary .coverage is useful. Could collect to `.coverage` then run `merge -f cobertura`. Two commands. Plan says collect -> .coverage, then merge -> xml. The merge also validates output. Later acceptance same.

`COVERAGE_TOOL ?= Microsoft.CodeCoverage.Console.exe` (from PATH after vcvars). Check presence: `which` at parse if coverage goals/toolchain needed. On Windows `where`. Error message tells to run from Developer environment.

But note `NO_TOOLCHAIN_GOALS` includes coverage; outer coverage doesn't need cl. Inner sub-make `cov-inputs` needs cl and will error if missing. The coverage tool check: add `coverage` to toolchain needs? If inner make sees `cov-inputs`, NEEDS_TOOLCHAIN yes; it checks cl. CodeCoverage check can be in coverage branch recipe: `ifeq ($(call which,Microsoft.CodeCoverage.Console.exe),)` → error at parse when coverage goal in COVERAGE=1 mode. But `which` defers? It's `$(shell ...)` evaluated at parse; only if conditional. Use `ifeq` inside `ifeq COVERAGE,1` and only when goal coverage? Simpler check in recipe via a `cov-tool-check` phony target. Or at parse: if `COVERAGE=1` and `PLATFORM=windows`, check tool exists (because any cov run needs it). But direct `COVERAGE=1 unit` shouldn't need collector. So check only when goal is coverage. `$(filter coverage,$(MAKECMDGOALS))`. Fine.

6. `cov-inputs` dependencies: only unit exes.
- Add `UNIT_EXES` variable in template.
- Phony:
```
cov-inputs: $(UNIT_EXES) $(BUILD_DIR)/common/c/ppm_io_test$(EXE) $(BUILD_DIR)/common/cpp/ppm_io_test$(EXE)
```
But `UNIT_EXES` built via template; common tests appended manually.
- Note: on Windows test exes must be linked with /PROFILE. LDFLAGS global includes it. Good.

7. `cov-reset`:
```
cov-reset:
	$(call RMFILE,$(UNIT_MARKERS))
	$(call RMTREE,$(COV_DIR))
	<delete .gcda under BUILD_DIR on gcc> 
```
On Windows `del /S /Q $(native $(BUILD_DIR))\*.coverage` maybe. Since COV_DIR removed, no need. On GCC remove `*.gcda` in BUILD_DIR: POSIX `find $(BUILD_DIR) -name '*.gcda' -delete`; but RMFILE? define `RMGLOB`? Could simply `$(RMTREE,$(BUILD_DIR))`? Too heavy (rebuild). Add platform command `RMDATA`:
- Windows: `if exist ... del /S /Q ...\*.gcda` (no gcda on Windows, harmless).
- POSIX: `find $(BUILD_DIR) -name '*.gcda' -delete`.
Better define `RMDATA = ...` per platform. Or since variant is isolated, coverage dispatcher could `clean` the cov variant and rebuild every time—simplest and guarantees fresh data. Cost: full rebuild of unit exes only (not all apps/refs) — moderate but fine; unit-only coverage build is small (common + 4 tasks core). This also ensures /PROFILE flags applied. "coverage should always work" favors clean. But incremental convenience? Coverage runs are occasional. Recommend: `cov-reset` removes markers + data (not all objects); no need full rebuild. But .gcda deletion necessary only GCC. Use `find`.

8. `cov-report`:
- Windows: merge `.coverage` -> cobertura; output summary from merge? The tool prints summaries? `merge` may print report summary. Could also echo path. No threshold.
- Linux: `gcovr --root . --object-directory $(BUILD_DIR) --gcov-executable gcov$(GCC_SUFFIX) --filter ... --exclude ... --xml coverage.xml --txt summary.txt` plus console.
  - gcovr version? Need user confirmation but plan can use common flags. `--object-directory` may not be needed if run from root; gcovr searches build. Use `--gcov-object-directory`? The option is `--object-directory DIR` (alias `-o`? no, -o is output). In gcovr, `-r/--root`, `--object-directory`. Confidence medium; they can validate.
  - gcovr needs .gcno/.gcda; builds in build dir. `--filter` multiple.
- Report location `$(BUILD_DIR)/coverage/`.

9. Tests marker semantics: after collect run, `unit` markers created. `cov-report` should verify markers exist? Make itself succeeded if sub-make returns 0. If collector masks exit, make's own exit is inside collect. If collect returns 0 despite failing make, markers for failed test absent but target `unit` would have failed inside make. We could post-check count: all UNIT_MARKERS exist. Add `cov-report` dependency/check: `$(UNIT_MARKERS)` as order-only? If missing, make would try to build them (rerun) outside collector. Better recipe check with shell:
```
	$(if $(wildcard ...),, error)
```
Need ensure. Plan mentions postcondition.

But user says "coverage should always work"; if a test fails, coverage target should fail. Add explicit check in `cov-report`: verify each marker exists and coverage file exists; else `exit /b 1`. Could implement via make `$(if $(filter-out ...))` at parse? Markers list known. At recipe time `$(wildcard $(UNIT_MARKERS))` gives existing; compare words. `$(if $(filter-out $(wildcard $(UNIT_MARKERS)),$(UNIT_MARKERS)),$(error ...))` would error at recipe expansion. Or shell command. Use a `cov-check` target. Plan-level detail enough.

10. Windows settings:
- content:
```xml
<Configuration>
  <CodeCoverage>
    <ModulePaths>
      <IncludeDirectories>
        <Directory Recursive="true">C:\...\build\...-cov</Directory>
      </IncludeDirectories>
    </ModulePaths>
    <Sources>
      <Exclude>
        <Source>.*_test\.(c|cpp)$</Source>
      </Exclude>
    </Sources>
    <CollectFromChildProcesses>True</CollectFromChildProcesses>
    <EnableStaticNativeInstrumentation>True</EnableStaticNativeInstrumentation>
    <EnableDynamicNativeInstrumentation>False</EnableDynamicNativeInstrumentation>
  </CodeCoverage>
</Configuration>
```
- Test-source regex path uses backslashes; regex `_test\.(c|cpp)$` should match. Note case-insensitive.
- Should exclude `ref`? Unit phase no refs built. If later, add.
- Generate via `$(file ...)` or prechecked template? Since no docs changes, a checked-in `coverage/coverage.runsettings` template with relative dir might be simpler, but path absolute needed. Generate in build dir. Use `$(file >...)` with a `define`. Must handle comma in XML? no commas. Text includes `|` inside regex `(c|cpp)`—fine in make. `$` no. Backslashes in regex: `\.` inside make variable stays; `$(file)` writes literal. XML path with `\` from native. Good. But `$(file ...)` in recipe expands before shell; make may interpret `#`? no. Newlines in define preserved. This is clever but needs testing. Alternative use a settings template with `<Directory Recursive="true">$(BUILD_DIR_NATIVE)</Directory>` substituted through `$(file)`. Fine.

input.newString:
# =============================================================================
#  Покрытие: вариант *-cov, только unit-тесты. На выходе — один Cobertura XML
#  на обеих платформах: $(COV_XML).
#
#  Схема: cov-inputs (только тестовые exe) -> cov-reset (маркеры и старые
#  данные) -> unit под сбором -> cov-report. Сброс маркеров обязателен:
#  иначе make не перезапустит тесты и покрытие останется пустым.
# =============================================================================
COV_DIR      := $(BUILD_DIR)/coverage
COV_XML      := $(COV_DIR)/coverage.cobertura.xml
COV_SETTINGS := $(COV_DIR)/coverage.runsettings
COV_MARKERS  := $(UNIT_MARKERS)
COV_MARKERS_NATIVE := $(foreach m,$(COV_MARKERS),$(call native,$m))

ifeq ($(PLATFORM),windows)
  COV_CHECK_MARKERS = for %%M in ($(COV_MARKERS_NATIVE)) do if not exist "%%M" exit /b 1
else
  COV_CHECK_MARKERS = for m in $(COV_MARKERS); do test -f "$$m" || exit 1; done
endif

# Настройки статической инструментации C++: искать бинарники только в
# каталоге варианта и исключить из отчёта исходники самих тестов.
define COV_SETTINGS_XML
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<Configuration>
  <CodeCoverage>
    <ModulePaths>
      <IncludeDirectories>
        <Directory Recursive="true">$(call native,$(CURDIR)/$(BUILD_DIR))</Directory>
      </IncludeDirectories>
    </ModulePaths>
    <Sources>
      <Exclude>
        <Source>.*_test\.(c|cpp)</Source>
      </Exclude>
    </Sources>
    <EnableStaticNativeInstrumentation>True</EnableStaticNativeInstrumentation>
    <EnableDynamicNativeInstrumentation>False</EnableDynamicNativeInstrumentation>
    <CollectFromChildProcesses>True</CollectFromChildProcesses>
  </CodeCoverage>
</Configuration>
endef

# $(MAKE) спрятан в переменной: иначе make считает строку рекурсивной и
# исполняет её даже при make -n.
COV_TEST_CMD = $(MAKE) COVERAGE=1 unit

ifeq ($(TOOLCHAIN),msvc)
  ifneq ($(and $(filter 1,$(COVERAGE)),$(filter coverage,$(MAKECMDGOALS))),)
    ifeq ($(call which,Microsoft.CodeCoverage.Console.exe),)
      $(error Не найден Microsoft.CodeCoverage.Console.exe. Запустите make из Developer-окружения (vcvars64.bat).)
    endif
  endif
else
  ifneq ($(and $(filter 1,$(COVERAGE)),$(filter coverage,$(MAKECMDGOALS))),)
    ifeq ($(call which,$(GCOV)),)
      $(error Не найден $(GCOV). Установите gcov, совпадающий с компилятором.)
    endif
    ifeq ($(call which,$(GCOVR)),)
      $(error Не найден $(GCOVR). Установите gcovr.)
    endif
  endif
endif

cov-inputs: $(UNIT_EXES)

cov-reset:
	$(call RMTREE,$(COV_DIR))
	$(call RMMARKERS,$(COV_MARKERS_NATIVE))
	$(RMDATA)

cov-settings:
	$(call MKDIR,$(COV_DIR))
	$(file >$(COV_SETTINGS),$(COV_SETTINGS_XML))

ifeq ($(TOOLCHAIN),msvc)
cov-report:
	$(COV_CHECK_MARKERS)
	$(call CHECKNONEMPTY,$(COV_XML))
else
cov-report:
	$(COV_CHECK_MARKERS)
	$(COV_GCOVR_CMD)
	$(call CHECKNONEMPTY,$(COV_XML))
endif

ifeq ($(filter 1,$(COVERAGE)),1)
coverage:
	$(MAKE) COVERAGE=1 cov-inputs
	$(MAKE) COVERAGE=1 cov-reset
ifeq ($(TOOLCHAIN),msvc)
	$(MAKE) COVERAGE=1 cov-settings
	"$(COVERAGE_TOOL)" collect --nologo --settings "$(call native,$(COV_SETTINGS))" --output "$(call native,$(COV_XML))" --output-format cobertura $(COV_TEST_CMD)
else
	$(MAKE) COVERAGE=1 unit
endif
	$(MAKE) COVERAGE=1 cov-report
else
coverage:
	$(MAKE) COVERAGE=1 coverage
endif

+      $(error Не найден $(GCOVR). Установите gcovr.)
+    endif
+  endif
+endif
+
+cov-inputs: $(UNIT_EXES)
+
+cov-reset:
+	$(call RMTREE,$(COV_DIR))
+	$(call RMMARKERS,$(COV_MARKERS_NATIVE))
+	$(RMDATA)
+
+cov-settings:
+	$(call MKDIR,$(COV_DIR))
+	$(file >$(COV_SETTINGS),$(COV_SETTINGS_XML))
+
+ifeq ($(TOOLCHAIN),msvc)
+cov-report:
+	$(COV_CHECK_MARKERS)
+	$(call CHECKNONEMPTY,$(COV_XML))
+else
+cov-report:
+	$(COV_CHECK_MARKERS)
+	$(COV_GCOVR_CMD)
+	$(call CHECKNONEMPTY,$(COV_XML))
+endif
+
+ifeq ($(filter 1,$(COVERAGE)),1)
 coverage:
-	$(error coverage — задел: COVERAGE=1 уже задаёт флаги и ограничения варианта)
+	$(MAKE) COVERAGE=1 cov-inputs
+	$(MAKE) COVERAGE=1 cov-reset
+ifeq ($(TOOLCHAIN),msvc)
+	$(MAKE) COVERAGE=1 cov-settings
+	"$(COVERAGE_TOOL)" collect --nologo --settings "$(call native,$(COV_SETTINGS))" --output "$(call native,$(COV_XML))" --output-format cobertura $(COV_TEST_CMD)
+else
+	$(MAKE) COVERAGE=1 unit
+endif
+	$(MAKE) COVERAGE=1 cov-report
+else
+coverage:
+	$(MAKE) COVERAGE=1 coverage
+endif

parts.text:
Why did cov-settings recipe not print? Because when make expands the recipe for printing under -n, it executes `$(file)` which fails. It maybe printed nothing because expansion of `$(call MKDIR)`? It should print `if not exist...`. Unless make's -n suppresses? The sub-make may not receive -n? It did for prior. Actually `make[1]: Entering` then immediate error; maybe the first line expanded to a command but make didn't print because it aborts during expansion of the second line? Make expands all recipe lines for a target before printing/executing them. Yes! GNU make expands the entire recipe (all lines) before executing, to handle `$(MAKE)` recursion etc. Thus `$(file)` executes during expansion of second line, before first line runs, so directory doesn't exist. This is true even in normal mode: `$(file)` writes during recipe expansion before any commands execute. So MKDIR hasn't run yet. That's the real bug, not just dry-run.

Fix: Ensure directory exists at parse time or in a separate sub-make invocation before cov-settings. Since coverage invokes `$(MAKE) COVERAGE=1 cov-settings` separately after cov-inputs (which creates variant dirs but not COV_DIR). Could make `cov-settings` depend on a directory order-only prerequisite `| $(COV_DIR)/`; make builds directory target before running recipe, and then `$(file)` expansion occurs after prerequisite built. But recipe expansion happens after prerequisites are updated, yes. So add `cov-settings: | $(COV_DIR)/`. Then MKDIR prerequisite creates dir before recipe expansion. Then remove MKDIR line or keep. That solves normal mode. Under `make -n`, prerequisite `$(COV_DIR)/` recipe also not executed (dry run), so `$(file)` still fails. Need guard against DRY_RUN.

Also `$(file)` writes during expansion even in dry run. So guard:
```
ifeq ($(DRY_RUN),)
cov-settings: | $(COV_DIR)/
	$(file >$(COV_SETTINGS),$(COV_SETTINGS_XML))
else
cov-settings: | $(COV_DIR)/
endif
```
But `$(COV_DIR)/` target recipe under -n prints mkdir but doesn't execute, then no file write. Good. In normal mode, order-only prerequisite ensures dir created, then file function writes. But note: `$(file)` expansion for all recipe lines happens after prerequisites built. Great.

However `$(file)` writes an empty recipe line; after expansion, make sees empty command and does nothing. Fine.

Need also ensure `cov-settings` target is not considered "nothing to be done" incorrectly: `$(file)` side effect with no shell command; target phony, so always runs. Good.

Let's edit. Also the `MKDIR` line in cov-settings can be removed if order-only. Use:
```
cov-settings: | $(COV_DIR)/
ifeq ($(DRY_RUN),)
	$(file >$(COV_SETTINGS),$(COV_SETTINGS_XML))
endif
```
Can an `ifeq` appear between target and recipe? Yes conditionals parsed, recipe lines attach. Under dry run, no recipe lines => phony target with no recipe; make says nothing to be done? Phony always considered. Fine.

But `$(COV_DIR)/` target exists via `%/:` pattern; path `build/.../coverage/` matches `%/` with stem `build/.../coverage`; recipe MKDIR. Good.

Now another issue observed: UNIT markers are named `ppm_test.exe.passed` for task tests, not `ppm_test.passed`. Wait look at `cov-reset` output: `01-image-gen\c\ppm_test.exe.passed`. Why? In TASK_template:
```
TEST_$1_$2 := .../name$(EXE)
UNIT := $(patsubst %$(EXE),%,$$(TEST)).passed
```
`patsubst %$(EXE),%` with EXE=.exe should strip `.exe`; why output has `.exe.passed`? Because in eval, `$$(TEST_$1_$2)` expansion yields `...ppm_test.exe`, then `patsubst %.exe,%`? The pattern `%$(EXE)` -> `%.exe`, replacement `%`; should strip. But output shows `.exe.passed`, so `EXE` in `$(patsubst %$(EXE),%...)` maybe empty? In TASK_template definition, `$(EXE)` is expanded when eval is called; EXE=.exe. Hmm. Wait `UNIT_$1_$2 := $(patsubst %$(EXE),%,$$(TEST_$1_$2)).passed`. At eval time, `TEST_...` is deferred `$$(...)`; the patsubst argument `$$(TEST_...)` contains literal `$(TEST...)`, not the path, so patsubst can't match. So it returns `$(TEST_...).passed`, then later expands to `...ppm_test.exe.passed`. Ah existing bug: markers are `exe.passed` on Windows. Not our concern; COV_MARKERS uses actual UNIT_MARKERS, so reset loop correct. On Linux UNIT markers are `name.passed`? Since `$$(TEST)` deferred, patsubst leaves it, then `.passed` -> `name.passed` (because EXE empty). So Windows markers append `.passed` to `.exe`. Fine, existing behavior. Our reset handles.

But wait `UNIT_EXES += $$(TEST_$1_$2)` gives exes. Good.

Now fix cov-settings.

CMP    = fc /B $(call native,$1) $(call native,$2)
  RUN    = $(call native,$1)
  NUL    = NUL
  TOUCH  = type nul > $(call native,$1)
  # Точный код возврата. `if errorlevel N` значит «>= N», поэтому сначала
  # отсекаем всё больше ожидаемого, затем добираем остаток до него.
  CHECK0  =
  CHECK64 = & if errorlevel 65 exit /b 1 & if errorlevel 64 exit /b 0 & exit /b 1
  CHECK65 = & if errorlevel 66 exit /b 1 & if errorlevel 65 exit /b 0 & exit /b 1
  CHECK66 = & if errorlevel 67 exit /b 1 & if errorlevel 66 exit /b 0 & exit /b 1
  # Непустой stderr. Под cmd переменную цикла for пишем как %%A: make отдаёт
  # рецепт в cmd, где один % начинает подстановку и превращается в пусто.
  NONEMPTY = for %%A in ($(call native,$(ERR))) do if %%~zA==0 exit /b 1
  RMMARKERS = for %%M in ($1) do if exist "%%M" del /F /Q "%%M"
  RMDATA =
  CHECKFILE = if not exist "$(call native,$1)" exit /b 1
  CHECKNONEMPTY = if not exist "$(call native,$1)" exit /b 1 & for %%A in ("$(call native,$1)") do if %%~zA==0 exit /b 1
  which = $(shell where $1 2>nul)
else
  SHELL := /bin/sh
  native = $1
  MKDIR  = mkdir -p $1
  RMFILE = rm -f $1
  RMTREE = rm -rf $1
  CP     = cp -f $1 $2
  CMP    = cmp $1 $2
  RUN    = $1
  NUL    = /dev/null
  TOUCH  = touch $1
  CHECK0  =
  CHECK64 = ; test $$? -eq 64
  CHECK65 = ; test $$? -eq 65
  CHECK66 = ; test $$? -eq 66
  NONEMPTY = test -s $(ERR)
  RMMARKERS = rm -f $1
  RMDATA = find $(BUILD_DIR) -name '*.gcda' -delete
  CHECKFILE = test -f $1
  CHECKNONEMPTY = test -s $1
  which = $(shell command -v $1 2>/dev/null)
endif

9. C/C++ parity: C uses `static int clamp`; C++ `std::clamp`. Both same. But out-of-domain behavior differs? C `hsv_to_rgb` fmod on negative; C++ std::abs same. C++ `static_cast<int>` same. Probably parity.

Our report has duplicate classes. This is a coverage infrastructure issue: per-module duplicates mean overall rate understated. Need fix/justify. - h=359.999 -> near red (255,0,0 after truncation? hue 359.999 gives r≈255, g=0, b≈0, likely 255,0,0)

- h=-60 or 420 wrap behavior? Current code: -60/60=-1, `(int)-1 % 6 = -1` -> no case -> r1=g1=b1=0, m=v-c; result black-ish (v-c), not hue wrap. 420 -> 7%6=1 -> yellow? 420-360=60 yes. 720 -> 12%6=0 red. Negative fails. If hue contract [0,360], okay, but h=360 accepted. Should document.

- NaN/inf: `static_cast<int>(NaN)` UB in C++; C cast also UB. Input contract should exclude. Could mention not testing NaN/infinity or add validation upstream. Important potential bug but out of scope.

## Что значит «агрегация по `filename`»

Это объединение нескольких `<class>`-записей Cobertura, относящихся к одному и тому же исходному файлу, в одну логическую запись **до** подсчёта процентов.

В нашем отчёте один файл встречается много раз. Например, `common/cpp/ppm_io.cpp` идёт отдельными классами с разными результатами:

```text
ppm_io.cpp rate=0
ppm_io.cpp rate=0.0555
ppm_io.cpp rate=0.5
ppm_io.cpp rate=1
...
```

Причина: каждый тестовый exe — отдельный модуль, и в каждый слинкована своя копия `ppm_io.obj`. `Microsoft.CodeCoverage.Console` собирает покрытие по модулям и не сливает одинаковые исходники. В итоге одна и та же строка исходника учитывается столько раз, сколько тестовых бинарников её содержат.

Агрегация по `filename` делает так:

1. Берёт все классы с одинаковым нормализованным путём (`C:\...\common\cpp\ppm_io.cpp`).
2. Для каждого номера строки объединяет данные:
   - `valid` — строка существует;
   - `hits` — например, `max(hits_1, hits_2, ...)` для факта покрытия или сумма, если нужны реальные счётчики;
   - строка считается покрытой, если она покрыта **хотя бы в одной** копии.
3. Пересчитывает `line-rate` уже по объединённому набору строк.
4. Опционально оставляет в XML один `<class>` на файл.

Важно: это не усреднение процентов. Нельзя складывать `0.0` и `1.0` и получать `0.5`. Нужно объединить **множества строк**, а потом считать `covered / valid`.

Почему без этого общий процент врёт:

- файл, слинкованный в 10 тестов, учитывается 10 раз;
- копии, где модуль не использовался, дают нули и тянут итог вниз;
- один и тот же исходник одновременно имеет и 0%, и 100%, что для оценки кода бессмысленно;
- общий `line-rate=0.3769` в нашем XML — это не покрытие проекта, а сумма по модулям с дублями.

Оговорка: если один и тот же файл компилируется с разными макросами/флагами, агрегация только по имени может скрыть различия. В нашем случае флаги одинаковые, поэтому ключ `filename` корректен. [ФАКТ, ВЫСОКИЙ]

# dotnet-coverage code coverage tool - .NET CLI - .NET | Microsoft Learn

**This article applies to:** ✔️ .NET 8 SDK and later versions

## Synopsis

```console
dotnet-coverage <command> [-h, --help] [--version]
```

## Description

The `dotnet-coverage` tool:

- Enables the cross-platform collection of code coverage data of a running process.
- Provides cross-platform merging of code coverage reports.

## Options

- **`-h|--help`**

    Shows command-line help.
- **`--version`**

    Displays the version of the dotnet-coverage utility.

## Install

To install the latest release version of the `dotnet-coverage`[NuGet package](https://www.nuget.org/packages/dotnet-coverage), use the [dotnet tool install](../tools/dotnet-tool-install) command:

```dotnetcli
dotnet tool install --global dotnet-coverage
```

## Commands

| Command |
| --- |
| dotnet-coverage merge |
| dotnet-coverage collect |
| dotnet-coverage connect |
| dotnet-coverage snapshot |
| dotnet-coverage shutdown |
| dotnet-coverage instrument |
| dotnet-coverage uninstrument |

## dotnet-coverage merge

The `merge` command is used to merge several code coverage reports into one. This command is available on all platforms. This command supports the following code coverage report formats:

- `coverage`
- `cobertura`
- `xml`

### Synopsis

```console
dotnet-coverage merge
    <files>...
    [--remove-input-files]
    [-o|--output <output>] [-f|--output-format <output-format>]
    [-l|--log-file <log-file>] [-ll|--log-level <log-level>]
    [-dco|--disable-console-output] [--nologo]
    [-?|-h|--help]
```

### Arguments

- **`<files>`**

    The input code coverage reports.

### Options

- **`--remove-input-files`**

    Removes all input coverage reports that were merged.
- **`-r, --recursive`**

    .NET 7 SDK and earlier versions only Search for coverage reports in subdirectories.
- **`-o|--output <output>`**

    Sets the code coverage report output file.
- **`-f|--output-format <output-format>`**

    The output file format. Supported values: `coverage`, `xml`, and `cobertura`. Default is `coverage` (binary format that can be opened in Visual Studio).
- **`-l|--log-file <log-file>`**

    Sets the log file path. When you provide a directory (with a path separator at the end), a new log file is generated for each process under analysis.
- **`-ll|--log-level <log-level>`**

    Sets the log level. Supported values: `Error`, `Info`, and `Verbose`.
- **`-dco|--disable-console-output`**

    Disables console output.
- **`--nologo`**

    Do not display Code Coverage banner.

## dotnet-coverage collect

The `collect` command is used to collect code coverage data for any .NET process and its subprocesses. For example, you can collect code coverage data for a console application or a Blazor application. This command supports dynamic and static instrumentation. Static instrumentation is available on all platforms. You can specify files to be statically instrumented using `include-files` option. Dynamic instrumentation is available on Windows (x86, x64 and Arm64), Linux (x64), and macOS (x64). The command supports only .NET modules. Native modules are not supported.

### Synopsis

The `collect` command can run in two modes.

#### Command Mode

The `collect` command will collect code coverage for the given process executed by the `command` argument.

```console
dotnet-coverage collect
    <command> <args>...
    [-s|--settings <settings>] [-id|--session-id <session-id>]
    [-if|--include-files <include-files>] [-o|--output <output>] [-f|--output-format <output-format>]
    [-l|--log-file <log-file>] [-ll|--log-level <log-level>]
    [-dco|--disable-console-output] [--nologo]
    [-?|-h|--help]
```

#### Server Mode

The `collect` command hosts a server for code coverage collection. Clients can connect to the server via `connect` command.

```console
dotnet-coverage collect
    [-s|--settings <settings>] [-id|--session-id <session-id>]
    [-sv|--server-mode] [-b|--background] [-t|--timeout]
    [-if|--include-files <include-files>] [-o|--output <output>] [-f|--output-format <output-format>]
    [-l|--log-file <log-file>] [-ll|--log-level <log-level>]
    [-dco|--disable-console-output] [--nologo]
    [-?|-h|--help]
```

### Arguments

- **`<command>`**

    The command for which to collect code coverage data.
- **`<args>`**

    The command line arguments for the command.

### Options

- **`-s|--settings <settings>`**

    Sets the path to the XML code coverage settings.
- **`-id|--session-id <session-id>`**

    Specifies the code coverage session ID. If not provided, the tool will generate a random GUID.
- **`-sv|--server-mode`**

    Starts the collector in server mode. Clients can connect to the server with the `connect` command.
- **`-b|--background`**

    Starts code coverage collection server in a new background process. Clients can connect to the server with the `connect` command.
- **`-t|--timeout`**

    Timeout (in milliseconds) for interprocess communication between clients and the server.
- **`-if|--include-files <include-files>`**

    Specifies list of files to be statically instrumented.
- **`-o|--output <output>`**

    Sets the code coverage report output file.
- **`-f|--output-format <output-format>`**

    The output file format. Supported values: `coverage`, `xml`, and `cobertura`. Default is `coverage` (binary format that can be opened in Visual Studio).
- **`-l|--log-file <log-file>`**

    Sets the log file path. When you provide a directory (with a path separator at the end), a new log file is generated for each process under analysis.
- **`-ll|--log-level <log-level>`**

    Sets the log level. Supported values: `Error`, `Info`, and `Verbose`.
- **`-dco|--disable-console-output`**

    Disables console output.
- **`--nologo`**

    Do not display Code Coverage banner.

## dotnet-coverage connect

The `connect` command is used to connect with the existing server and collects code coverage data for any .NET process and its subprocesses. For example, you can collect code coverage data for a console application or a Blazor application. The command supports only .NET modules. Native modules are not supported.

Note

Command will use dynamic instrumentation for all subprocesses which is available on Windows (x86, x64 and Arm64), Linux (x64), and macOS (x64). If you need to statically instrument any .NET module use `instrument` command (with corresponding session ID option) before executing `connect` command.

### Synopsis

```console
dotnet-coverage connect
    <session> <command> <args>...
    [-b|--background] [-t|--timeout]
    [-l|--log-file <log-file>] [-ll|--log-level <log-level>]
    [-dco|--disable-console-output] [--nologo]
    [-?|-h|--help]
```

### Arguments

- **`<session>`**

    The session ID of the server hosted by the `collect` command.
- **`<command>`**

    The command for which to collect code coverage data.
- **`<args>`**

    The command line arguments for the command.

### Options

- **`-b|--background`**

    Starts the client in a new background process.
- **`-t|--timeout`**

    Timeout (in milliseconds) for interprocess communication between the client and the server.\* **`-l|--log-file <log-file>`**
- **`-l|--log-file <log-file>`**

    Sets the log file path. When you provide a directory (with a path separator at the end), a new log file is generated for each process under analysis.
- **`-ll|--log-level <log-level>`**

    Sets the log level. Supported values: `Error`, `Info`, and `Verbose`.
- **`-dco|--disable-console-output`**

    Disables console output.
- **`--nologo`**

    Do not display Code Coverage banner.

## dotnet-coverage snapshot

Creates a coverage file for existing code coverage collection.

### Synopsis

```console
dotnet-coverage snapshot
    <session>
    [-r|--reset]
    [-tn|--tag-name <tag-name>] [-tid|--tag-identifier <tag-identifier>]
    [-o|--output <output>]
    [-t|--timeout]
    [-l|--log-file <log-file>] [-ll|--log-level <log-level>]
    [-dco|--disable-console-output] [--nologo]
    [-?|-h|--help]
```

### Arguments

- **`<session>`**

    The session ID of the collection for which a coverage file is to be generated.

### Options

- **`-r|--reset <reset>`**

    Clears existing coverage information after a coverage file is created.
- **`-tn|--tag-name <tag-name>`**

    Creates a snapshot tag name in the coverage file with current coverage information. Tag-name and tag-identifier are mutually inclusive.
- **`-tid|--tag-identifier <tag-identifier>`**

    Creates a snapshot tag identifier in the coverage file with current coverage information. Tag-name and tag-identifier are mutually inclusive.
- **`-o|--output <output>`**

    Sets the code coverage report output file. If not provided, it's generated automatically with a timestamp.
- **`-t|--timeout`**

    Timeout (in milliseconds) for interprocess communication between the client and the server.
- **`-l|--log-file <log-file>`**

    Sets the log file path. When you provide a directory (with a path separator at the end), a new log file is generated for each process under analysis.
- **`-ll|--log-level <log-level>`**

    Sets the log level. Supported values: `Error`, `Info`, and `Verbose`.
- **`-dco|--disable-console-output`**

    Disables console output.
- **`--nologo`**

    Do not display Code Coverage banner.

## dotnet-coverage shutdown

Closes existing code coverage collection.

### Synopsis

```console
dotnet-coverage shutdown
    <session>
    [-t|--timeout]
    [-l|--log-file <log-file>] [-ll|--log-level <log-level>]
    [-dco|--disable-console-output] [--nologo]
    [-?|-h|--help]
```

### Arguments

- **`<session>`**

    The session ID of the collection to be closed.

### Options

- **`-t|--timeout`**

    Timeout (in milliseconds) for interprocess communication with the server.
- **`-l|--log-file <log-file>`**

    Sets the log file path. When you provide a directory (with a path separator at the end), a new log file is generated for each process under analysis.
- **`-ll|--log-level <log-level>`**

    Sets the log level. Supported values: `Error`, `Info`, and `Verbose`.
- **`-dco|--disable-console-output`**

    Disables console output.
- **`--nologo`**

    Do not display Code Coverage banner.

## dotnet-coverage instrument

The instrument command is used to instrument binary on disk.

### Synopsis

```console
dotnet-coverage instrument
    <input-file>
    [-s|--settings <settings>] [-id|--session-id <session-id>]
    [-o|--output <output>]
    [-l|--log-file <log-file>] [-ll|--log-level <log-level>]
    [-dco|--disable-console-output] [--nologo]
    [-?|-h|--help]
```

### Arguments

- **`<input-file>`**

    The input binary.

### Options

- **`-s|--settings <settings>`**

    Sets the path to the XML code coverage settings.
- **`-id|--session-id <session-id>`**

    Specifies the code coverage session ID. If not provided, the tool will generate a random GUID.
- **`-o|--output <output>`**

    Sets the path to output file binary. If not provided, instrumentation will be performed in-place.
- **`-l|--log-file <log-file>`**

    Sets the log file path. When you provide a directory (with a path separator at the end), a new log file is generated for each process under analysis.
- **`-ll|--log-level <log-level>`**

    Sets the log level. Supported values: `Error`, `Info`, and `Verbose`.
- **`-dco|--disable-console-output`**

    Disables console output.
- **`--nologo`**

    Do not display Code Coverage banner.

## dotnet-coverage uninstrument

The uninstrument command is used to restore original binary from the instrumented binary.

### Synopsis

```console
Microsoft.CodeCoverage.Console uninstrument
    <input-file>
    [-s|--settings <settings>]
    [-l|--log-file <log-file>] [-ll|--log-level <log-level>]
    [-dco|--disable-console-output] [--nologo]
    [-?|-h|--help]
```

### Arguments

- **`<input-file>`**

    The input instrumented binary.

### Options

- **`-s|--settings <settings>`**

    Sets the path to the XML code coverage settings.
- **`-l|--log-file <log-file>`**

    Sets the log file path. When you provide a directory (with a path separator at the end), a new log file is generated for each process under analysis.
- **`-ll|--log-level <log-level>`**

    Sets the log level. Supported values: `Error`, `Info`, and `Verbose`.
- **`-dco|--disable-console-output`**

    Disables console output.
- **`--nologo`**

    Do not display Code Coverage banner.

## Sample scenarios

## Collecting code coverage

Collect code coverage data for any .NET application (such as console or Blazor) by using the following command:

```console
dotnet-coverage collect dotnet run
```

In case of an application that requires a signal to terminate, you can use Ctrl+C, which will still let you collect code coverage data. For the argument, you can provide any command that will eventually start a .NET app. For example, it can be a PowerShell script.

### Sessions

When you're running code coverage analysis on a .NET server that just waits for messages and sends responses, you need a way to stop the server to get final code coverage results. You can use Ctrl+C locally, but not in Azure Pipelines. For these scenarios, you can use sessions. You can specify a session ID when starting collection, and then use the `shutdown` command to stop collection and the server.

For example, assume you have a server in the *D:\serverexample\server* directory and a test project in the *D:\serverexample\tests* directory. Tests are communicating with the server through the network. You can start code coverage collection for the server as follows:

```console
D:\serverexample\server> dotnet-coverage collect --session-id serverdemo "dotnet run"
```

Session ID was specified as `serverdemo`. Then you can run tests as follows:

```console
D:\serverexample\tests> dotnet test
```

A code coverage file for session `serverdemo` can be generated with current coverage as follows:

```console
dotnet-coverage snapshot --output after_first_test.coverage serverdemo
```

Also, a snapshot tag can be added to the coverage file using tag options as follows:

```console
dotnet-coverage snapshot --tag-name after_first_test --tag-identifier after_first_test serverdemo
```

Finally, session `serverdemo` and the server can be closed as follows:

```console
dotnet-coverage shutdown serverdemo
```

Following is an example of full output on the server side:

```console
D:\serverexample\server> dotnet-coverage collect --session-id serverdemo "dotnet run"
SessionId: serverdemo
Waiting for a connection... Connected!
Received: Hello!
Sent: HELLO!
Waiting for a connection... Code coverage results: output.coverage.
D:\serverexample\server>
```

### Server and client mode

Code coverage collection can be done in server-client mode as well. In this scenario, a code coverage collection server starts, and multiple clients can connect with the server. Code coverage is collected for all the clients collectively.

Start the code coverage server using the following command:

```condole
dotnet-coverage collect --session-id serverdemo --server-mode
```

In this example, the session ID was specified as `serverdemo` for the server. A client can connect to the server using this session ID using the following command:

```condole
dotnet-coverage connect serverdemo dotnet run
```

Finally, you can close the session `serverdemo` and the server using the following command:

```console
dotnet-coverage shutdown serverdemo
```

The server process creates a collective code coverage report for all clients and exits.

Following is an example of full output on the server side:

```console
D:\serverexample\server> dotnet-coverage collect --session-id serverdemo --server-mode
SessionId: serverdemo
// Server will be in idle state and wait for connect and shutdown commands
Code coverage results: output.coverage.
D:\serverexample\server>
```

Following is an example of full output on the client side:

```console
D:\serverexample\server> dotnet-coverage connect serverdemo ConsoleApplication.exe World
Hello World!!
D:\serverexample\server> dotnet-coverage connect serverdemo WpfApplication.exe
D:\serverexample\server> dotnet-coverage shutdown serverdemo
D:\serverexample\server>
```

You can also start both server and client in background mode. Another process starts in the background and returns control back to the user.

Following is an example of full output in background server client mode:

```console
D:\serverexample\server> dotnet-coverage collect --session-id serverdemo --server-mode --background
D:\serverexample\server> dotnet-coverage connect --background serverdemo ConsoleApplication.exe World
D:\serverexample\server> dotnet-coverage connect --background serverdemo WpfApplication.exe
D:\serverexample\server> dotnet-coverage shutdown serverdemo
D:\serverexample\server>
```

## Static code coverage for managed assemblies

The dotnet-coverage tool can be used to collect code coverage for managed assemblies using static instrumentation. There are three different methods available that you can use. To demonstrate, let's assume we have a simple C# console application:

```console
D:\examples\ConsoleApp> dotnet run
Hello, World!
```

### Use collect command with include files option or configuration

If you don't want to use the `instrument` command, then the files to be instrumented can be specified using `--include-files` option as follows:

```console
D:\examples\ConsoleApp> dotnet-coverage collect --include-files .\bin\Debug\net9.0\*.dll dotnet run
dotnet-coverage v17.14.1.0 [win-x64 - .NET 9.0.2]

SessionId: 57862ec0-e512-49a5-8b66-2804174680fc
Hello, World!
Code coverage results: output.coverage.
```

You can also specify files to be instrumented using configuration as follows:

```xml
<ModulePaths>
  <IncludeDirectories>
    <Directory>D:\examples\ConsoleApp\bin\Debug\net7.0</Directory>
  </IncludeDirectories>
</ModulePaths>
```

### Using instrument and collect commands

In this case, first binary needs to be instrumented as follows:

```console
D:\examples\ConsoleApp> dotnet-coverage instrument .\bin\Debug\net7.0\ConsoleApp.dll
dotnet-coverage v17.14.1.0 [win-x64 - .NET 9.0.2]

Input file successfully instrumented.
```

Then you can collect code coverage as follows:

```console
D:\examples\ConsoleApp> dotnet-coverage collect .\bin\Debug\net7.0\ConsoleApp.exe
dotnet-coverage v17.14.1.0 [win-x64 - .NET 9.0.2]

SessionId: a09e6bef-ff64-4b5f-8bb8-fc495ebb50ba
Hello, World!
Code coverage results: output.coverage.
```

### Use the instrument and collect commands in server mode

In this case, you can completely separate coverage collection from running your application. First, instrument your binary as follows:

```console
D:\examples\ConsoleApp> dotnet-coverage instrument --session-id 73c34ce5-501c-4369-a4cb-04d31427d1a4 .\bin\Debug\net7.0\ConsoleApp.dll
dotnet-coverage v17.14.1.0 [win-x64 - .NET 9.0.2]

Input file successfully instrumented.
```

Note

Session ID needs to be used in this scenario to make sure that the application can connect and provide data to external collector.

In the second step, you need to start coverage collector as follows:

```console
D:\examples\ConsoleApp> dotnet-coverage collect --session-id 73c34ce5-501c-4369-a4cb-04d31427d1a4 --server-mode
dotnet-coverage v17.14.1.0 [win-x64 - .NET 9.0.2]

SessionId: 73c34ce5-501c-4369-a4cb-04d31427d1a4
```

Then the application can be started as follows:

```console
D:\examples\ConsoleApp> .\bin\Debug\net7.0\ConsoleApp.exe
Hello, World!
```

Finally, the collector can be closed as follows:

```console
D:\examples\ConsoleApp> dotnet-coverage shutdown 73c34ce5-501c-4369-a4cb-04d31427d1a4
dotnet-coverage v17.14.1.0 [win-x64 - .NET 9.0.2]
```

### Settings

You can specify a file with settings when you use the `collect` command. The settings file can be used to exclude some modules or methods from code coverage analysis. The format is the same as the data collector configuration inside a *runsettings* file. For more information, see [Customize code coverage analysis](/en-us/visualstudio/test/customizing-code-coverage-analysis). Here's an example:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<Configuration>
    <CodeCoverage>
        <!--
        Additional paths to search for .pdb (symbol) files. Symbols must be found for modules to be instrumented.
        If .pdb files are in the same folder as the .dll or .exe files, they are automatically found. Otherwise, specify them here.
        Note that searching for symbols increases code coverage run time. So keep this small and local.
        -->
        <SymbolSearchPaths>
            <Path>C:\Users\User\Documents\Visual Studio 2012\Projects\ProjectX\bin\Debug</Path>
            <Path>\\mybuildshare\builds\ProjectX</Path>
        </SymbolSearchPaths>

        <!--
        About include/exclude lists:
        Empty "Include" clauses imply all; empty "Exclude" clauses imply none.
        Each element in the list is a regular expression (ECMAScript syntax). See /visualstudio/ide/using-regular-expressions-in-visual-studio.
        An item must first match at least one entry in the include list to be included.
        Included items must then not match any entries in the exclude list to remain included.
        -->

        <!-- Match assembly file paths: -->
        <ModulePaths>
            <Include>
                <ModulePath>.*\.dll$</ModulePath>
                <ModulePath>.*\.exe$</ModulePath>
            </Include>
            <Exclude>
                <ModulePath>.*CPPUnitTestFramework.*</ModulePath>
            </Exclude>
            <!-- Additional directories from .NET assemblies should be statically instrumented: -->
            <IncludeDirectories>
                <Directory Recursive="true">C:\temp</Directory>
            </IncludeDirectories>
        </ModulePaths>

        <!-- Match fully qualified names of functions: -->
        <!-- (Use "\." to delimit namespaces in C# or Visual Basic, "::" in C++.)  -->
        <Functions>
            <Exclude>
                <Function>^Fabrikam\.UnitTest\..*</Function>
                <Function>^std::.*</Function>
                <Function>^ATL::.*</Function>
                <Function>.*::__GetTestMethodInfo.*</Function>
                <Function>^Microsoft::VisualStudio::CppCodeCoverageFramework::.*</Function>
                <Function>^Microsoft::VisualStudio::CppUnitTestFramework::.*</Function>
```

## Merge code coverage reports

You can merge `a.coverage` and `b.coverage` and store the data in `merged.coverage` as follows:

```console
dotnet-coverage merge -o merged.coverage a.coverage b.coverage
```

For example, if you run a command like `dotnet test --collect "Code Coverage"`, the coverage report is stored into a folder that is named a random GUID. Such folders are hard to find and merge. Using this tool, you can merge all code coverage reports for all your projects using globbing patterns as follows:

```console
dotnet-coverage merge -o merged.cobertura.xml -f cobertura **\*.coverage
```

The preceding command merges all coverage reports from the current directory and all subdirectories and stores the result into a cobertura file. In Azure Pipelines, you can use [Publish Code Coverage Results task](/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/tasks/test/publish-code-coverage-results) to publish a merged cobertura report.

You can use the `merge` command to convert a code coverage report to another format. For example, the following command converts a binary code coverage report into XML format.

```console
dotnet-coverage merge -o output.xml -f xml input.coverage
```

## Telemetry

Starting with version 18.10.0, the `dotnet-coverage` tool collects telemetry data to help Microsoft improve the code coverage tools. The data records which commands you run and which options you set when you run the tool. You can disable telemetry at any time. For more information about the data that's collected and how to opt out, see [Microsoft.CodeCoverage.Console telemetry](/en-us/visualstudio/test/microsoft-code-coverage-console-tool-telemetry).

The `merge` command takes a directory containing `.cov` files and produces a combined code coverage report. In PHPCOV 13.0, this works reliably even when the individual files were generated on different machines (for instance, in parallel CI jobs) or using different PHPUnit installation methods (PHAR vs. Composer). The merged result can be written in any of the supported report formats: Clover XML, OpenClover XML, Cobertura XML, Crap4j XML, HTML, plain text, or PHPUnit's XML format.

A typical CI workflow for merging code coverage from parallel test runs looks like this:

1. Each CI job runs PHPUnit with `--coverage-php /path/to/directory/$(uuidgen).cov --include-git-information`
2. The `.cov` files from all jobs are collected into a single directory, for example `/path/to/directory`
3. `phpcov merge --html report /path/to/directory` produces a combined HTML report in the directory `report` from the files in `/path/to/directory`"

## Эксперимент с `merge` — подробный сценарий

По документации `Microsoft.CodeCoverage.Console merge` поддерживает входные отчёты в `coverage`, `cobertura` и `xml` и умеет писать `cobertura`. [ФАКТ, ВЫСОКИЙ] Но не описано, схлопывает ли он **одинаковые `filename` внутри одного отчёта**. Это и есть главный вопрос эксперимента.

### 0. Подготовка

Работаем только в `build/` или временном каталоге, исходный отчёт не трогаем.

```powershell
$raw  = 'build\msvc-debug-dynamic-obj-none-cov\coverage\coverage.cobertura.xml'
$work = 'C:\Users\vboxuser\AppData\Local\Temp\opencode\coverage-merge'
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $work | Out-Null
Copy-Item $raw "$work\raw.cobertura.xml"
```

### 1. Зафиксировать baseline

До `merge` считаем по `raw.cobertura.xml`:

- число `<class>`;
- число уникальных `filename`;
- список файлов с дублями и сколько раз каждый повторяется;
- сумму `lines-valid`/`lines-covered` по всем классам;
- агрегированное объединение по `filename` (для каждой строки — `max(hits)`);
- корневые `lines-valid`, `lines-covered`, `line-rate`.

Это нужно, чтобы понять, что именно изменил `merge`, а не сравнивать «на глаз».

Ожидаемая картина по текущему отчёту: классов заметно больше, чем уникальных файлов; `ppm_io.cpp`/`ppm_io.c` повторяются; корневой `line-rate` считается по всем копиям.

### 2. `merge` одного отчёта

```powershell
Microsoft.CodeCoverage.Console.exe merge --nologo `
  -f cobertura -o "$work\merged-single.xml" "$work\raw.cobertura.xml"
```

Проверяем:

1. Команда вообще принимает один Cobertura-файл.
2. Сколько `<class>` и уникальных `filename` в результате.
3. Исчезли ли дубли `ppm_io.cpp`.
4. Совпадает ли корневой `line-rate` с независимым объединением строк.
5. Сохранились ли `<methods>` и `<line>`.
6. Как объединены `hits`: `max`, сумма или что-то ещё.
7. Нормализованы ли пути: регистр, `/` vs `\`, абсолютные/относительные.

Возможные исходы:

- **A. Дубли схлопнулись, проценты пересчитаны.** Это идеальный вариант: `merge` становится обязательным шагом без своего парсера.
- **B. Дубли остались, но отчёт валиден.** `merge` — только конвертер, не агрегатор.
- **C. Один файл не принимается.** Пробуем два входа, в том числе два одинаковых.

### 3. `merge` двух одинаковых отчётов

```powershell
Microsoft.CodeCoverage.Console.exe merge --nologo `
  -f cobertura -o "$work\merged-two.xml" `
  "$work\raw.cobertura.xml" "$work\raw.cobertura.xml"
```

Смотрим:

- удвоились ли `lines-valid`/`lines-covered`/`hits`;
- не появились ли ещё дубли;
- не изменился ли `line-rate`.

Это отвечает на вопрос: можно ли собирать отдельный отчёт на каждый тестовый exe, а потом сливать их через `merge`.

### 4. Синтетический минимальный тест

Это самый чистый способ понять семантику. Создаём два крошечных Cobertura-файла с одним и тем же `filename`:

`a.xml`:

```xml
<coverage line-rate="0.5" branch-rate="0" lines-covered="1" lines-valid="2">
  <packages><package name="p" line-rate="0.5" branch-rate="0">
    <classes>
      <class name="a" filename="C:\repo\a.c" line-rate="0.5" branch-rate="0">
        <methods/>
        <lines>
          <line number="1" hits="1"/>
          <line number="2" hits="0"/>
        </lines>
      </class>
    </classes>
  </package></packages>
</coverage>
```

`b.xml` — тот же файл, но строка 1 с `hits="0"`, строка 2 с `hits="1"`.

Проверяем:

```powershell
merge -f cobertura -o "$work\ab.xml" "$work\a.xml" "$work\b.xml"
```

Ожидаемый правильный результат: один `<class filename="C:\repo\a.c">`, обе строки покрыты, `lines-covered=2`, `lines-valid=2`, `line-rate=1`.

Дополнительно проверяем:

- `hits` при разных значениях: `5` и `7` — что получится, `7` или `12`;
- вариант с двумя `<class>` для одного `filename` **внутри одного файла** — схлопнет ли;
- пути `C:\repo\a.c`, `C:/repo/a.c`, `c:\repo\a.c` — считает ли их одним файлом;
- битый XML и пустой файл — возвращает ли ненулевой код.

### 5. Round-trip через `.coverage`

Если Cobertura-вход ведёт себя странно, проверяем бинарный путь:

```powershell
merge -f coverage  -o "$work\raw.coverage"     "$work\raw.cobertura.xml"
merge -f cobertura -o "$work\roundtrip.xml"    "$work\raw.coverage"
```

Смотрим, не теряются ли строки/методы и не появляется ли агрегация. Это запасной вариант, если Cobertura-вход поддерживается только формально.

### 6. Критерий решения

| Результат | Что делаем |
|---|---|
| `merge` схлопывает дубли и пересчитывает проценты | Добавляем `merge` в `coverage`: `collect` → `raw.cobertura.xml` → `merge` → `coverage.cobertura.xml` → проверка порога |
| `merge` агрегирует только между отчётами | Рассматриваем сбор отдельного отчёта на каждый тестовый exe и `merge` по ним; оцениваем число запусков и время |
| `merge` не агрегирует | Нужен отдельный постпроцессор. PowerShell вы исключили — остаётся C++-exe с тестами или внешний `ReportGenerator` |
| `merge` теряет методы/строки | Для отчёта не годится, даже если проценты считает |

### Порог 80%: A + B

Предлагаю двухуровневую схему:

- **жёсткий gate:** общий агрегированный `line-rate >= 80%`;
- **обязательный обзор:** отдельный список файлов с покрытием ниже 80%; по каждому — либо тесты, либо письменное обоснование, почему это допустимо.

Это соответствует вашему «общий агрегированный, но каждый низкий случай разбирать». Если позже захотите сделать per-file 80% жёстким, это отдельное решение.

### `help`/`version`

Согласен: не перехватываем stdout. Регрессию формата ловит acceptance, а локализация — отдельный слой тестирования. Следствие: `parse_args.c` остаётся около 73%, и **жёсткий per-file порог 80% для него невозможен** без тестов вывода, переноса функций в `main.c` или исключения функций из покрытия. Поэтому per-file 80% пока только обзор, не gate.

### `clamp`

Если clamp — часть гарантии, контракт должен быть сформулирован явно. Нужно выбрать:

- **C1:** `h∈[0;360]`, `s,v∈[0;1]`; clamp — защита от нарушения предусловия, не тестируется;
- **C2:** для любых конечных `h,s,v` результат гарантированно в `[0;255]`; clamp тестируется, включая нижнюю и верхнюю границы.

При C2 нужно отдельно решить, что делать с отрицательным hue: сейчас `switch ((int)(h/60) % 6)` для отрицательного hue не попадает ни в один case, и цвет получается не «поворотом hue», а вырожденным. Если гарантия только по диапазону RGB — это допустимо, но поведение цвета надо описать. Если нужен корректный wrap — это уже правка алгоритма.

## 3. C2 и «заворачиваем»

«Заворачиваем hue» — это нормализация оттенка по модулю 360 перед выбором сектора:

```c
h = fmod(h, 360.0);
if (h < 0)
    h += 360.0;
```

Примеры:

- `h = -60` → `300` (фиолетовый сектор);
- `h = 420` → `60` (жёлтый);
- `h = 360` → `0` (красный).

Сейчас положительные значения больше 360 уже работают через `(int)(h / 60.0) % 6`, а отрицательные — нет: `-60 / 60 = -1`, `-1 % 6 = -1`, `switch` не попадает ни в один `case`, и получается вырожденный цвет. В C и C++ `%` для отрицательных одинаковый, так что поведение совпадает, но оно не «заворачивает» hue.

Разница контрактов:

- **C2 только про диапазон RGB:** для любых конечных `h,s,v` результат в `[0;255]`, clamp тестируется. Отрицательный hue может давать странный цвет, но диапазон гарантирован. Заворачивать не нужно, точные цвета для `-60` не проверяем.
- **C2 с нормализацией hue:** для любых конечных `h` оттенок корректно заворачивается. Тогда меняем обе реализации (`hsv_to_rgb.c` и `.cpp`) и проверяем точные цвета для `-60`, `420`, `720`.

Нужно выбрать, что именно входит в гарантию.

cv::COLOR_BGR2XYZ, cv::COLOR_RGB2XYZ, cv::COLOR_XYZ2BGR, cv::COLOR_XYZ2RGB
## RGB \\(\\leftrightarrow\\) YCrCb JPEG (or YCC) \\\[Y \\leftarrow 0.299 \\cdot R + 0.587 \\cdot G + 0.114 \\cdot B\\] \\\[Cr \\leftarrow (R-Y) \\cdot 0.713 + delta\\] \\\[Cb \\leftarrow (B-Y) \\cdot 0.564 + delta\\] \\\[R \\leftarrow Y + 1.403 \\cdot (Cr - delta)\\] \\\[G \\leftarrow Y - 0.714 \\cdot (Cr - delta) - 0.344 \\cdot (Cb - delta)\\] \\\[B \\leftarrow Y + 1.773 \\cdot (Cb - delta)\\] where \\\[delta = \\left \\{ \\begin{array}{l l} 128 & \\mbox{for 8-bit images} \\\\ 32768 & \\mbox{for 16-bit images} \\\\ 0.5 & \\mbox{for floating-point images} \\end{array} \\right .\\] Y, Cr, and Cb cover the whole value range.

On output \\(0 \\leq V \\leq 1\\), \\(0 \\leq S \\leq 1\\), \\(0 \\leq H \\leq 360\\) . The values are then converted to the destination data type: - 8-bit images: \\(L \\leftarrow L\*255/100, \\; a \\leftarrow a + 128, \\; b \\leftarrow b + 128\\) - 16-bit images: (currently not supported) - 32-bit images: L, a, and b are left as is
See also
cv::COLOR_BGR2Lab, cv::COLOR_RGB2Lab, cv::COLOR_Lab2BGR, cv::COLOR_Lab2RGB
## RGB \\(\\leftrightarrow\\) CIE L\*u\*v\* In case of 8-bit and 16-bit images, R, G, and B are converted to the floating-point format and scaled to fit 0 to 1 range. \\\[\\vecthree{X}{Y}{Z} \\leftarrow \\vecthreethree{0.412453}{0.357580}{0.180423}{0.212671}{0.715160}{0.072169}{0.019334}{0.119193}{0.950227} \\cdot \\vecthree{R}{G}{B}\\] \\\[L \\leftarrow \\fork{116\*Y^{1/3} - 16}{for \\(Y>0.008856\\)}{903.3 Y}{for \\(Y\\leq 0.008856\\)}\\] \\\[u' \\leftarrow 4\*X/(X + 15\*Y + 3 Z)\\] \\\[v' \\leftarrow 9\*Y/(X + 15\*Y + 3 Z)\\] \\\[u \\leftarrow 13\*L\*(u' - u\_n) \\quad \\text{where} \\quad u\_n=0.19793943\\] \\\[v \\leftarrow 13\*L\*(v' - v\_n) \\quad \\text{where} \\quad v\_n=0.46831096\\] This outputs \\(0 \\leq L \\leq 100\\), \\(-134 \\leq u \\leq 220\\), \\(-140 \\leq v \\leq 122\\) . The values are then converted to the destination data type: - 8-bit images: \\(L \\leftarrow 255/100 L, \\; u \\leftarrow 255/354 (u + 134), \\; v \\leftarrow 255/262 (v + 140)\\) - 16-bit images: (currently not supported) - 32-bit images: L, u, and v are left as is Note that when converting integer Luv images to RGB the intermediate X, Y and Z values are truncated to \\( \[0, 2] \\) range to fit white point limitations. ## Bayer \\(\\rightarrow\\) RGB The Bayer pattern is widely used in CCD and CMOS cameras. It enables you to get color pictures from a single plane where R, G, and B pixels (sensors of a particular component) are interleaved as follows: ![Bayer\_patterns.png](https://docs.opencv.org/3.4.20/Bayer_patterns.png) Bayer patterns (BGGR, GBRG, GRGB, RGGB) The output RGB components of a pixel are interpolated from 1, 2, or 4 neighbors of the pixel having the same color.
Note
See the following for information about correspondences between OpenCV Bayer pattern naming and classical Bayer pattern naming.
![bayer.png](https://docs.opencv.org/3.4.20/bayer.png) Bayer pattern There are several modifications of the above pattern that can be achieved by shifting the pattern one pixel left and/or one pixel up. The two letters \\(C\_1\\) and \\(C\_2\\) in the conversion constants CV\_Bayer \\(C\_1 C\_2\\) 2BGR and CV\_Bayer \\(C\_1 C\_2\\) 2RGB indicate the particular pattern type. ## Нормализация hue — да, это локальная правка

Для `hsv_to_rgb` это не архитектура, а локальное приведение входа в домен:

```c
h = fmod(h, 360.0);
if (h < 0)
    h += 360.0;
```

То же в C++ через `std::fmod`.

Это делает функцию периодической по hue:

- `-60` → `300` → magenta;
- `-300` → `60` → yellow;
- `420` → `60` → yellow;
- `720` → `0` → red;
- `360` → `0` → red.

Меняется только `hsv_to_rgb.c/.cpp` и тесты. Контракт и поведение — локальные.

## Про OpenCV и `H = H + 360`

В документации OpenCV это правило стоит **в преобразовании RGB → HSV**, где `H` вычисляется из RGB и заведомо ограничен формулой. Там одного `+360` достаточно, потому что исходное значение не улетает произвольно далеко. [ФАКТ, ВЫСОКИЙ]

Для публичной функции, которая принимает произвольный `double hue`, `H + 360` недостаточно:

- `-720 + 360 = -360` — всё ещё отрицательно;
- `1080` — всё ещё больше 360.

Поэтому для произвольного входа нужна нормализация по модулю, а не одно сложение. `fmod` + коррекция отрицательного остатка даёт `[0;360)`. Это соответствует смыслу hue как угла, но не является дословным повторением OpenCV-кода.

Если хочется сохранить `360` как отдельное значение, можно оставить `[0;360]`, но `360` и `0` всё равно дают один цвет. Проще зафиксировать `[0;360)`.

## Публичный API: какое поведение ожидать

Нужно явно записать контракт в заголовке. Варианты:

**Вариант 1 — hue периодический, s/v в стандартном диапазоне:**

```text
@pre  std::isfinite(h), 0 <= s <= 1, 0 <= v <= 1
@post 0 <= r,g,b <= 255
h нормализуется по модулю 360; 360 эквивалентно 0.
```

Тогда clamp — защита от нарушения предусловия, а не часть гарантии.

**Вариант 2 — hue периодический, s/v любые конечные, clamp — часть гарантии:**

```text
@pre  std::isfinite(h), std::isfinite(s), std::isfinite(v)
@post 0 <= r,g,b <= 255
h нормализуется по модулю 360; выходные компоненты насыщаются в [0;255].
```

Тогда тесты на `s=2`, `v=2` обязательны, строки clamp покрываются.

**Вариант 3 — жёсткие предусловия, никакой нормализации:**

```text
@pre  0 <= h <= 360, 0 <= s <= 1, 0 <= v <= 1
```

Выход за диапазон — нарушение контракта, поведение не гарантируется.

Я бы выбрал **вариант 1 или 2**, но не 3: hue — угловая величина, и периодичность — естественная часть модели. Вопрос только в том, входит ли clamp в гарантию для s/v вне `[0;1]`.

`NaN`/`inf` в любом варианте лучше исключить предусловием: `static_cast<int>(NaN)` — UB, и покрывать это тестами бессмысленно.

## Архитектурная ли это правка

Сама нормализация hue — **нет**. Это локальное изменение функции и тестов.

Аудит контрактов во всех задачах — это уже **design/quality pass**, но не обязательно архитектура. Архитектурной правка становится, если меняются:

- границы валидации (например, перенос проверки размера из `main` в `parse_args`);
- модель ошибок (возврат `std::expected` вместо `RGB`, коды ошибок);
- публичные сигнатуры;
- владение ресурсами.

Для `hsv_to_rgb` ничего из этого не нужно: достаточно `@pre/@post` в заголовке и тестов. Для остальных задач стоит пройти тем же чек-листом позже, отдельным проходом:

- какие предусловия у `luma`, `pixel_word`, `ppm_read`, `filter`?
- что гарантируется на выходе?
- где сейчас живёт валидация — в парсере, в `main` или в модуле?
- нет ли функций, которые обещают больше, чем проверяют?

Это не требует нового модуля или фреймворка. Если по итогам аудита окажется, что валидация размазана по `main` и парсерам, вот тогда это архитектурная правка границ ответственности.

# =============================================================================

#  на обеих платформах: $(COV_XML).
#
#  Схема: cov-inputs (только тестовые exe) -> cov-reset (маркеры и старые
#  данные) -> unit под сбором -> cov-report. Сброс маркеров обязателен:
#  иначе make не перезапустит тесты и покрытие останется пустым.
# =============================================================================
COV_DIR      := $(BUILD_DIR)/coverage
COV_XML      := $(COV_DIR)/coverage.cobertura.xml
COV_SETTINGS := $(COV_DIR)/coverage.runsettings
COV_MARKERS  := $(UNIT_MARKERS)
COV_MARKERS_NATIVE := $(foreach m,$(COV_MARKERS),$(call native,$m))

ifeq ($(PLATFORM),windows)
  COV_CHECK_MARKERS = for %%M in ($(COV_MARKERS_NATIVE)) do if not exist "%%M" exit /b 1
else
  COV_CHECK_MARKERS = for m in $(COV_MARKERS); do test -f "$$m" || exit 1; done
endif

# Настройки статической инструментации C++: искать бинарники только в
# каталоге варианта и исключить из отчёта исходники самих тестов.
define COV_SETTINGS_XML
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<Configuration>
  <CodeCoverage>
    <ModulePaths>
      <IncludeDirectories>
        <Directory Recursive="true">$(call native,$(CURDIR)/$(BUILD_DIR))</Directory>
      </IncludeDirectories>
    </ModulePaths>
    <Sources>
      <Exclude>
        <Source>.*_test\.(c|cpp)</Source>
      </Exclude>
    </Sources>
    <EnableStaticNativeInstrumentation>True</EnableStaticNativeInstrumentation>
    <EnableDynamicNativeInstrumentation>False</EnableDynamicNativeInstrumentation>
    <CollectFromChildProcesses>True</CollectFromChildProcesses>
  </CodeCoverage>
</Configuration>
endef

# $(MAKE) спрятан в переменной: иначе make считает строку рекурсивной и
# исполняет её даже при make -n.
COV_TEST_CMD = $(MAKE) PLATFORM=$(PLATFORM) COVERAGE=1 unit

ifeq ($(TOOLCHAIN),msvc)
  ifneq ($(and $(filter 1,$(COVERAGE)),$(filter coverage,$(MAKECMDGOALS))),)
    ifeq ($(call which,Microsoft.CodeCoverage.Console.exe),)
      $(error Не найден Microsoft.CodeCoverage.Console.exe. Запустите make из Developer-окружения (vcvars64.bat).)
    endif
  endif
else
  ifneq ($(and $(filter 1,$(COVERAGE)),$(filter coverage,$(MAKECMDGOALS))),)
    ifeq ($(call which,$(GCOV)),)
      $(error Не найден $(GCOV). Установите gcov, совпадающий с компилятором.)
    endif
    ifeq ($(call which,$(GCOVR)),)
      $(error Не найден $(GCOVR). Установите gcovr.)
    endif
  endif
endif

cov-inputs: $(UNIT_EXES)

cov-reset:
	$(call RMTREE,$(COV_DIR))
	$(call RMMARKERS,$(COV_MARKERS_NATIVE))
	$(RMDATA)

# $(file ...) срабатывает при раскрытии рецепта, то есть до выполнения
# команд, поэтому каталог создаётся order-only пререквизитом. В dry-run

cov-settings: | $(COV_DIR)/
ifeq ($(DRY_RUN),)
	$(file >$(COV_SETTINGS),$(COV_SETTINGS_XML))
endif

ifeq ($(TOOLCHAIN),msvc)
cov-report:
	$(COV_CHECK_MARKERS)
	$(call CHECKNONEMPTY,$(COV_XML))
else
cov-report:
	$(COV_CHECK_MARKERS)
	$(COV_GCOVR_CMD)
	$(call CHECKNONEMPTY,$(COV_XML))

	$(MAKE) COVERAGE=1 cov-inputs

ifeq ($(TOOLCHAIN),msvc)
	$(MAKE) COVERAGE=1 cov-settings
	"$(COVERAGE_TOOL)" collect --nologo --settings "$(call native,$(COV_SETTINGS))" --output "$(call native,$(COV_XML))" --output-format cobertura $(COV_TEST_CMD)
else
	$(MAKE) COVERAGE=1 unit
endif
	$(MAKE) COVERAGE=1 cov-report
else
coverage:
	$(MAKE) COVERAGE=1 coverage
endif

## Ответ по merge

`coverage.cobertura.xml` — это raw. В нём:

- **5 packages** — по test-exe: `ppm_test`, `read_passport_test`, `ppm_stats_test`, `filter_test`, `ppm_io_test`;
- **87 `<class>`** — это типы и лямбды, а не 87 копий одного класса;
- **22 уникальных файла**;
- `ppm_io.cpp` встречается 45 раз = 9 классов × 5 test-exe. Это не дубли одной записи, а один и тот же исходник, скомпилированный в разные тестовые бинарники.

`merge` одного raw оставляет те же 87 классов, потому что имена классов разные. Он не объединяет строки по файлу.

Если агрегировать правильно — по ключу `(filename, line number)` и брать `hits > 0` при наличии хотя бы в одном классе — получается:

```text
1300 строк, 1029 покрыто, 79.15%
```

Для 80% нужно 1040 покрытых строк, то есть **+11**. Это честный baseline, а не 37.69% из корневого `line-rate`.

## Идея «закрепить `ppm_io` за модулем»

Настройками coverage это напрямую не делается:

- `Sources/Exclude` умеет исключать исходники по маскам, но глобально для запуска;
- `ModulePaths/IncludeDirectories` фильтрует бинарники, а не владельцев исходников;
- отображения «этот `.cpp` принадлежит только этому test-exe» в runsettings нет.

Можно сделать отдельные runsettings на каждый test-exe и исключать `ppm_io` везде, кроме `ppm_io_test`. Для самого `ppm_io` потерь не будет: `ppm_io_test` покрывает все его строки — C `254/302`, C++ `218/250`. Но:

- `luma` покрывается `filter_test`, `ppm_io_test`, `ppm_stats_test`;
- `int_token.h` — четырьмя разными тестами;
- для них «владелец» уже неочевиден, и назначение одного модуля потеряет реальные покрытые строки;
- появится N конфигураций, которые нужно синхронизировать при каждом новом тесте.

Поэтому закрепление исходника за модулем — не общее решение. Правильнее считать объединение строк по файлу. `coverage_check` не должен падать на повторяющихся `filename`: это нормальная структура отчёта. Он должен объединять `(filename, line)`.

Схему B с отдельным `collect` на каждый exe и `merge` можно не делать: текущий единый `collect` уже содержит все данные, а агрегатор их корректно объединит. `merge` пригодится только если понадобится отдельный нормализованный Cobertura-артефакт с одним классом на файл.

## Скорректированный план

1. **Hue**  
   Нормализация `h` по модулю 360 в C и C++. Контракт: конечные `h,s,v`, `h` периодичен, `s,v` насыщаются в `[0;1]`, выход в `[0;255]`. Тесты на `-60`, `-300`, `-360`, `360`, `420`, `720`, границы секторов и clamp.

2. **`parse_args`**  
   Перенос `n < 1 → PE_BADNUMBER` в `parse_args_old/new` для C и C++. Тесты `-5`, `0`, `--size -5`, `--size 0`. Guard `parse_args.c:49–50` удаляем. Верхняя граница `512` остаётся в `main`.

3. **`coverage_check`**  
   C++-exe: читает Cobertura, объединяет строки по `filename + line`, считает общий процент, проверяет `>= 80`, печатает файлы ниже 80. Повторяющийся `filename` — не ошибка. Тесты на синтетическом XML: ровно 80, ниже 80, несколько классов на один файл, пустой отчёт.

4. **Проверка**  
   После hue и `parse_args` — `make PLATFORM=windows coverage`, затем `coverage_check`. Смотрим, хватает ли 11 строк. Если после осмысленных тестов всё ещё ниже 80 — обсуждаем, какие тесты действительно нужны, а не исключаем файлы ради процента.

5. **Не делаем**  
   Аудит контрактов задач 2–4, правки README/AGENTS/CHANGELOG, Linux-прогон, PowerShell-постпроцессор.

## Следующий шаг

Начать с **hue + `parse_args`**: это небольшие локальные правки, они сразу меняют и код, и покрытие. После них реализовать `coverage_check` и прогнать отчёт.

`merge` и «закрепление `ppm_io` за модулем» в план не включаю: первый не объединяет строки, второй не обобщается на общие заголовки.
